stemMd: A hiking map is drawn at a scale of $1:250{,}000$, which means that $1$ centimeter on the map represents $250{,}000$ centimeters on the ground. Two shelters are $3.2$ centimeters apart on the map. What is the actual distance between the shelters, in kilometers? ($1$ kilometer $= 1{,}000$ meters and $1$ meter $= 100$ centimeters.)
explanationMd:
Scale the map distance first, then convert the units one step at a time so that no factor of $10$ goes missing.

Every map centimeter stands for $250{,}000$ ground centimeters, so

$$3.2 \times 250{,}000 = 800{,}000 \text{ centimeters}$$

Convert centimeters to meters by dividing by $100$:

$$800{,}000 \div 100 = 8{,}000 \text{ meters}$$

Convert meters to kilometers by dividing by $1{,}000$:

$$8{,}000 \div 1{,}000 = 8 \text{ kilometers}$$

A quick way to check: $1$ kilometer is $100{,}000$ centimeters, so $1$ map centimeter represents $250{,}000 \div 100{,}000 = 2.5$ kilometers. Then $3.2 \times 2.5 = 8$ kilometers, the same result.

The wrong choices all differ from the answer by a power of $10$, which is the signature of a unit conversion done with the wrong factor. Writing each conversion as its own line, with the unit named, is the habit that prevents it.

distractorRationale.a: This divides the $800{,}000$ centimeters by $1{,}000{,}000$, as if a meter held $1{,}000$ centimeters. One meter is $100$ centimeters, so the result is ten times too small.
distractorRationale.c: This divides the $800{,}000$ centimeters by only $10{,}000$, for instance by dividing by $10$ instead of $100$ when changing centimeters to meters. The result is ten times too large.
distractorRationale.d: This skips the centimeter-to-meter step and treats the $800{,}000$ ground centimeters as $800{,}000$ meters before dividing by $1{,}000$. The centimeters must first be divided by $100$.

accessibilityText: A map has a scale of 1 to 250,000, so 1 centimeter on the map represents 250,000 centimeters on the ground. Two shelters are 3.2 centimeters apart on the map. Find the actual distance in kilometers, given that 1 kilometer is 1,000 meters and 1 meter is 100 centimeters. The choices are 0.8, 8, 80 and 800.

provenance.notes: Original item. The scale and map distance were chosen so that the answer is a whole number and each distractor is the result of one specific wrong conversion factor.
